name: Town Center (Caracoles & the Plaza)
tagline: The walkable adobe heart of San Pedro
description: The compact grid around Caracoles street, the main plaza and the historic adobe church is where San Pedro's energy concentrates. Tour agencies, restaurants, bars, hostels and shops line dusty pedestrian-friendly streets, putting everything within a short stroll. It is convenient and lively, if touristy and pricier.
bestFor: First-timers who want to walk everywhere and book tours easily
pros: Everything within a short walk, including tours and dining
Easy to meet other travellers and join excursions
Best concentration of cafes, wifi spots and services
cons: Most touristy and expensive part of town
Can feel busy and dusty at peak hours

name: Solcor & Sequitor edges
tagline: Quieter adobe lanes on the town's fringe
description: Toward the Solcor and Sequitor ayllus, the town thins into calmer dirt lanes, small cabanas and guesthouses set among tamarugo trees and irrigation channels. It trades the buzz of Caracoles for silence and stars, a short walk or bike ride from the center, and often better value on longer stays.
bestFor: Slow travellers and stargazers wanting quiet and space
pros: Much quieter and darker for stargazing
Often better value on longer stays
Still walkable or a short bike to the center
cons: Wifi can be even more variable out here

name: Road toward Valle de la Luna
tagline: Desert-facing stays near the Valley of the Moon
description: Along the western road heading out toward the Valle de la Luna and the Cordillera de la Sal, a scattering of lodges and cabanas sit closer to open desert. You get sunset views over surreal salt formations and quick access to the valley, at the cost of being a drive or long bike from town.
bestFor: Photographers and those prioritising landscape over convenience
pros: Close to Valle de la Luna and stunning sunsets
Open desert scenery and big skies
Away from town noise and crowds
cons: Need a bike or vehicle for most trips into town
Very limited dining and shops nearby

name: Calama (nearby gateway city)
tagline: The practical regional hub with the airport
description: About 1.5 hours away, Calama is the mining city that serves as the region's transport and services hub, home to airport CJC, larger supermarkets, banks and more reliable connectivity. It lacks San Pedro's charm and desert magic, but works as a cheaper, better-connected base for errands, stocking up or steadier remote work.
bestFor: Nomads needing reliable wifi, supplies and the airport
pros: Airport CJC and long-distance transport connections
Bigger supermarkets, banks and generally cheaper goods
More reliable internet than San Pedro
cons: Little charm and far from the desert attractions
1.5-hour bus each way to reach San Pedro's sights
